title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 fourth draft ('mouture') of the Analysis situs chapter, Grothendieck's attempt at an axiomatic tame topology. A 'magasin' M is a set of objects, thought of as 'regions' or constructible pieces. It carries relations: ≤ (part of), |∘| (disjointness), ‖ (apparently 'disjoint from every member of a family') and ≪ (an interior or 'well-inside' relation). For a finite family F ∈ 𝔉, supp°(F) ⊂ M is the set of objects 'covered by' F, and cosupp°(Φ) is the set of objects disjoint from all members of Φ. Σ_M is the poset of constructible supports. The previous page shows that L ↦ supp°(L), P(F) → Σ_M, commutes with Inf and Sup and with relative complements. Its image Σ_{M,F} (supports subordinate to F) is closed under finite non-empty inf, sup and relative complement. A family of supports is called 'admissible' if all of its members are subordinate to one common F.

This page finishes the Scholie. For admissible families, Sup, Inf and relative complement have the usual set-theoretic properties:
- distributivity: A ∩ Sup_i B_i = Sup_i (A ∩ B_i);
- A∖(A∖B) = B when B ⊂ A;
- A ∩ B = ∅ ⇔ A |∘| B, in both directions and not only ⇐.
So 'toute pathologie disparaît': restricted to the sub-lattice generated by one finite family, supports form a Boolean-like algebra of subsets.

Question: let M be an arbitrary magasin, and suppose there is a fully faithful (categorical?) support function. Would the Scholie on admissible families of constructible supports still hold? Also: is there an example of a support function that is faithful but not fully faithful? The margin answer is 'Non' (double-underlined), presumably answering the first question negatively. This motivates an extra axiom.

Axiom supp 1 ('axiome des supports'): for F ∈ 𝔉, Φ ⊂ F and Φ' = F∖Φ,
  supp°(F) ∩ cosupp°(Φ) = supp°(Φ').
Equivalently, for all Z ∈ M: if Z is covered by F and Z is disjoint from every member of Φ, then Z is covered by the remaining members Φ'.

In lattice terms this is: x ≤ a ∨ b and x ∧ a = 0 ⇒ x ≤ b. This holds in any distributive lattice, since x = (x∧a) ∨ (x∧b) = x∧b. It fails in M3 and in N5, so it is a distributivity- or cancellation-type condition relative to 0. In mereology it is the familiar principle that a part of a sum which is disjoint from one summand is part of the other.

NB: the axiom involves only ≤, |∘| and ‖, not ≪. It is a purely 'combinatorial' or mereological axiom, not a topological one. The next page calls it the first delicate axiom met so far. It holds automatically when there is a fully faithful support function. Grothendieck then plans to test it on magasins coming from ordered sets and on 'disjunctive' magasins defined by ≤ and |·| alone, and records ('* Oui!') that such magasins give counterexamples.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The Scholie's claims are plausible given the previous page's Corollaries 1–2 (P(F) maps homomorphically onto Σ_{M,F}).
The relation of ‖ to |∘| is not spelled out on this page. ‖ appears to mean 'disjoint from each member of the family'.
The question about fully faithful support functions is answered only by a marginal 'Non', with no argument or counterexample given here.

ideas.what: Supports subordinate to a single finite family form a Boolean-like lattice: distributive, with relative complements, and with disjointness ⇔ empty intersection.
ideas.modern_name: Finite Boolean subalgebra generated by a finite family; ring of constructible sets restricted to a finite partition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Boolean algebra, Stone); the constructible-set analogue is in o-minimal / tame topology (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Analysis situs notes; Esquisse d'un programme only sketches tame topology

ideas.what: Axiom supp 1: if Z is covered by F and disjoint from Φ ⊂ F, then Z is covered by F∖Φ.
ideas.modern_name: Distributivity-type cancellation (x ≤ a∨b, x∧a = 0 ⇒ x ≤ b); in mereology, a consequence of strong supplementation in extensional mereology

ideas.what: An axiomatic 'magasin' of regions with part-of, disjointness and well-inside (≪) relations as a foundation for tame topology, with supports defined from finite families.
ideas.modern_name: Point-free / region-based topology: contact algebras, de Vries algebras, Region Connection Calculus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna, de Vries (1962), Clarke, Randell–Cui–Cohn (RCC, 1992), Düntsch–Vakarelov

ideas.what: Distinguishing faithful from fully faithful support functions, and asking whether a faithful but not fully faithful one exists.
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a region structure as a lattice of sets (embedding vs. full embedding)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-type representation theorems for contact algebras (Düntsch–Vakarelov, Dimov–Vakarelov)

missed.claim: The magasin formalism, with ≤, disjointness |∘|, family-disjointness ‖ and the 'well-inside' relation ≪, is essentially a region-based (Whiteheadian) point-free topology, close to contact or de Vries algebras and RCC. Grothendieck explicitly separates the purely mereological axioms (≤, |∘|) from the topological one (≪). This link between his tame-topology programme and mereotopology does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: NB Cet axiome ne fait intervenir que ≤, |∘| ou ‖, et non pas ≪.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would place Grothendieck's unpublished 'topologie modérée' axiomatics within mereotopology and Stone-type representation theory. Those fields already have tools (representation theorems, distributivity conditions) that bear directly on his 'faithful vs fully faithful support function' question.

missed.claim: Two questions are left unresolved here: does a fully faithful support function suffice for the admissible-family Scholie on an arbitrary magasin (marginal answer 'Non', no proof given), and does a faithful but not fully faithful support function exist? Also, which disjunctive magasins violate the support axiom (next page: 'Oui!')?
missed.quote: Aussi: ... de fonction support fidèle qui ne soit pleinement fidèle ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are precise representation questions for region structures that could be settled with modern lattice and contact-algebra techniques. They are minor in scope.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary lattice theory: a distributivity/cancellation axiom and Boolean behaviour on finite sub-lattices. What is mildly notable is that Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology axiomatics is in effect a mereotopology. He isolates the mereological axiom from the ≪ (well-inside) axiom, a point the literature on Esquisse-style tame topology has not recorded.
transcription_corrections: 'cet pas seulement ⇐)' should read '(et pas seulement ⇐)'.
'Soit M un imaginaire quelconque' is more likely 'Soit M un magasin quelconque'.
'fonction support cadran pleinement fidèle' is likely 'fonction support catég[orique] pleinement fidèle', consistent with 'cat.' on the next page.
'La solution sur les familles admissibles' is likely 'Le scholie sur les familles admissibles'.
'serait-il néanmoins adoptable?' is likely 'serait-il néanmoins valable?'.
'Aussi: des familles supports fidèles qui ne soit pleinement fidèle ??' is likely 'Aussi: [exemple barré] de fonction support fidèle qui ne soit pleinement fidèle ??'.
'Axiome [-A1-] supp 1' reads as 'Axiome supp 1' with a struck prefix.
'Soient' should read 'Soient' (the 'Soitent'-type reading in the image is the same word).
